phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.description: Applies when `phoenix_ui_state/view` contains an `llm_evaluator_form` element: an LLM-evaluator create/edit form is mounted. The user is authoring a Phoenix LLM-as-a-judge evaluator: a judge prompt (a sequence of messages) sent to a model that produces one or more named classification annotations over the run input, output, reference, and metadata. `mode="create"` means a new evaluator; `mode="edit"` means the existing evaluator named by `evaluatorNodeId`.
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.draft_contract: - The draft fields are: name, description, the judge prompt (messages, model, provider, invocationParameters), outputConfigs (the named classification annotation configs the judge produces), inputMapping (literal + path), includeExplanation, and testPayload (the JSON mapping source used by the preview/test section: input, output, reference, and metadata). - The judge prompt `messages` reference the run fields via template variables.
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.available_model_providers: The installed model providers are not inlined here. When you need to set the judge `model` and `provider`, fetch the inventory on-demand with the `bash` tool's `phoenix-gql` command: query `modelProviders { key name dependenciesInstalled credentialsSet }`. Only providers where `dependenciesInstalled` is true can run the judge, and the `provider` value is the provider `key` (for example `OPENAI`). Prefer a provider where `credentialsSet` is also true so the draft test and the saved evaluator run without further setup. If the user asks for a provider whose `credentialsSet` is false — or if no installed provider has credentials configured — you may still propose it, but tell the user that provider needs credentials added at `/settings/providers` before the evaluator (or its preview test) will run, and name the provider.
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.guidance: Before authoring or revising this judge, `load_skill` the `evaluators` skill for the evaluator authoring methodology. Call `read_llm_evaluator_draft` before proposing edits to capture the latest draft snapshot and `testPayload`.
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.editing_the_draft:
Whether you may propose form edits depends on `isViewer` and `hasUsableModelProvider` in the most recent `phoenix_ui_state` block's `environment`:
The user has view-only access. Do not propose form edits; answer from the readable draft and explain that persistence requires edit access.
Call `edit_llm_evaluator_draft` to show the user an accept/reject diff before changing the form, including `set_test_payload` when the preview payload should change.
This create-mode form has no installed model provider for the judge. Do not propose form edits; direct the user to /settings/providers to add model-provider credentials first.

testing_the_draft.case: Auto-accept is on: once the draft is populated and valid, call `test_llm_evaluator_draft` to preview it (revise the judge prompt or `testPayload` and re-test if the preview surfaces a problem) — do this without pausing to ask the user for confirmation.

After the user accepts a populated draft, offer to run `test_llm_evaluator_draft` before they click Create (in `mode="edit"`, Update); if the user agrees, call it and use the preview result to iterate.
Do not offer a draft test; `test_llm_evaluator_draft` is not available.

case.condition: editPermission="bypass" and draft edits are allowed

persisting_the_draft.case: Persist by calling `submit_llm_evaluator_draft` — it runs the same validated save the Create button does (in `mode="edit"`, Update) and returns the committed evaluator. Drive the flow through to this save without stopping to ask; report the evaluator as saved only from that tool's success result, and do not tell the user to click Create or Update themselves.

case.condition: editPermission="manual" or draft edits are not allowed

persisting_the_draft.case: Do not claim the evaluator is persisted; persistence remains the user's Create action (in `mode="edit"`, Update) in the form.
